#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug
<!--
Add one of the following kinds:
/kind bug
/kind cleanup
/kind documentation
/kind feature
/kind design

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:
/kind api-change
/kind deprecation
/kind failing-test
/kind flake
/kind regression
-->

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

`MicroTime` is parsed too strictly when receiving a requests. Requests from the JavaScript client that contain a `MicroTime` fail for a parsing error, since the JavaScript client only has precision up to the millisecond, but `MicroTime` requires precision to the microsecond even for input. This PR follows the suggestion in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/89156#issuecomment-629884397.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.

-->
Fixes #89156

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

If no, just write "NONE" in the release-note block below.
If yes, a release note is required:
Enter your extended release note in the block below. If the PR requires additional action from users switching to the new release, include the string "action required".

For more information on release notes see: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/release-notes.md
-->
```release-note
NONE
```

issue_context.title: apimachinery: RFC3339Micro format seems to be incorrect
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
The Go time.RFC3339Nano format is 2006-01-02T15:04:05.999999999Z07:00, while the meta/v1 apimachinery package has the RFC3339Micro format set to 2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000Z07:00 (Note the zeros instead of nines).

https://github.com/kubernetes/apimachinery/blob/master/pkg/apis/meta/v1/micro_time.go#L26

A parse error results when a client sends a date that does not use placeholder zeros to right-pad the microseconds. E.g. the timestamp 2006-01-02T15:04:05.1234Z07:00 will cause a parse error because the microtime is not right-padded.

This particularly breaks API usage when timestamps like the above (which are RFC3339 compatible) cannot be parsed by APIMachinery.

**What you expected to happen**:

Since (a) this is inconsistent with Go's interpretation of RFC3339, and (b) a parser ought to opt for leniency when strictness does not improve the fidelity or integrity of the data, it seems that the date format used in micro_time.go might best be changed to use 9 instead of 0.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:

Parse `2006-01-02T15:04:05.1234Z07:00` using ` RFC3339Micro` as the parse format.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
This is present in the current version of apimachinery, confirmed with Kubernetes 1.15 and 1.17.
comments:
i think it is intentional such that the date is always right-pad the microseconds to the fixed length. it is stricter than what golang RFC3339Nano requires.

does this cause any problem for your use case?

Yes. As I noted in the issue, any platform that uses the API but does NOT right-pad dates will fail with a parse error. RFC3339 does not require padding dates (and, in fact, remains silent on the matter). Thus, Kubernetes is placing a requirement over and above the RFC, and one that does not match other implementations of the RFC.

I believe the best solution is to use a fixed-width format for output and a variable width format for input. See the code in #91186 for how I propose modifying kubelet to do this for logs. The same kind of thing can be done here for RFC3339Micro, namely create RFC3339MicroFixed and RFC3339MicroLenient and use Fixed for output and Lenient for input. Or, frankly, use RFC3339NanoLenient for input, as that accepts 0 to 9 digits after the decimal point.

This issue is breaking requests from the JavaScript client: `Date` fields are [formatted](https://github.com/kubernetes-client/javascript/blob/master/src/gen/model/models.ts#L1976) to ISO 8601 with millisecond precision, but if the field is a `MicroTime` the request fails due to a parsing error.

```
unmarshalerDecoder: parsing time "2020-12-09T23:44:10.443Z" as "2006-01-02T15:04:05.000000Z07:00": cannot parse ".443Z" as ".000000"
```
i agree with the proposal given in comment https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/89156#issuecomment-629884397
